exposure: Placental edge distance from the internal cervical os (11-20 mm)
placental edge between 11 and 20 mm from the internal cervical os
cohort: 14 women with singleton pregnancies and a placental edge between 11 and 20 mm from the internal cervical os
finding: A placental edge distance of >10 mm from the internal cervical os, measured by transvaginal sonography near term, was associated with a high likelihood of successful vaginal delivery and a low risk of obstetrical hemorrhage.
mod_finding: This study found that a placental edge more than 10 mm from the internal os, as measured by transvaginal sonography near term, justified a trial of labor and carried a low risk of obstetrical hemorrhage.
